title: One-year W2 memory in 26 non-young dusty dwarf candidates exceeds controls but does not separate them from blends
abstract: We test year-scale time order in NEOWISE 2014-2024 visit measurements for the full published group of 26 non-young dwarf candidates with unblended-class extreme dust and W1-W2 excess above 0.3 mag. We remove a common control-star response and alternating-season means. The mean one-year W2 covariance divided by variance is 0.062. Its difference from magnitude- and visit-count-matched ordinary stars is 0.151, with a star bootstrap 95 percent interval of 0.021 to 0.271. But the difference from matched hot-colour blends is -0.018, with interval -0.143 to 0.102. These data do not resolve a difference from blends. A strict field-kinematics subset of 24 gives the same conclusion. Removing a linear trend weakens the excess over ordinary controls and gives an interval that includes zero. A Gaussian simulation checks the negative covariance introduced by seasonal mean fitting. This test supports slow source changes, but temporal memory alone does not locate the source or measure a dust lifetime. Limits include the small sample, statistical source classes, kinematic age proxies, measurement noise, local survey response and conditional reference matching. The bundle contains original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps.

display.caption: Observed W2 time-order statistics after common calibration and seasonal means are removed. Non-young candidates have more one-year memory than ordinary controls but no resolved difference from hot-colour blends. Linear detrending weakens the result.

citations.reason: Supplies all visit measurements, group labels and controls. We add a full-group time-order test with empirical blend comparisons.
Reports smooth infrared sources and population variability. We test memory without selecting smooth stars.
Earlier audit of variable-flux colours; our test addresses time order instead.
Prior extreme debris disc variability and dust-supply scenarios.
Survey documentation motivates seasonal and common-response controls.
